label: No COVID-19 Pandemic Occurs
detail: The coronavirus never spreads worldwide, so 2020 passes without a pandemic, lockdowns or a pandemic recession.
assumption: The pandemic and its economic and political effects are removed from the campaign; voters judge the President on the pre-2020 economy and other issues, and voting proceeds by ordinary rules.
facts_text: No new coronavirus has spread across the world in 2020, and there has been no pandemic, no stay-at-home orders and no closure of schools or businesses.
Unemployment remains low and the economy has kept growing through the year, and voting is held under ordinary rules.
research_questions: How have incumbents fared in past elections held during long periods of low unemployment and steady growth?
How did voters' views of the incumbent change in the 2020 polls before and after the pandemic began?
How did turnout and the choice of voting method change in 2020 compared with 2016 because of the pandemic?
How did presidents seeking reelection fare in years with no major national crisis?
source_text: There is no COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.
